text.content:
Detectives in cat ears. "We Never Sleep."

Headquarters: The Bridgehead (#28), Downtown, at the foot of the Coronado Bay Bridge. On the street: the Cattery
Industry: Private investigation and security
Leadership: Minako Arasaka, CEO since 2070. Founded by Michiko Arasaka (as Michiko Sanderson)
In Night City: About 600 staff, down from 1,800. The Puma Squad is its flagship field team
Dealing with edgerunners: Posted rates for walk-ins; one hard-luck case from Kabuki or Watson, told honestly, taken free

Everybody knows Danger Gal: the perky detective agency with the cat logo, the cartoon, the dolls and the Puma Squad, its photogenic crime-fighters. Fewer knew that behind the cartoon its founder spent decades hunting Arasaka's stay-behind agents across America for the US government.

Michiko's Agency (2025–2069)

Michiko Arasaka, Kei Arasaka's daughter, was seventeen in 2025 and about to be deported. She cut a deal with President Kress instead, took her mother's name, Sanderson, and built Danger Gal. The deal was with Kress personally; when Kress stepped down in 2053, Militech's friends in Washington cancelled Danger Gal's federal contracts, pulled its agents' licenses outside the Free States, and took the Puma Squad cartoon off NUSA networks. Michiko pulled back to Night City and kept hunting on her own money. In 2069 the NUSA seized what was left of her East Coast offices and opened her sealed file.

The Split (2070)

Michiko went home to Tokyo that winter. The family's price was everything Danger Gal had learned about Arasaka's people in America, and the agency's Art Deco Clock Tower in Downtown. Her daughter Minako refused to let the agency go with her: sign it over, or never hear from her daughter again. Michiko signed. The trademarks were already in Minako's name. - Michiko took the Clock Tower, the archives, the Arasaka files, and the agents loyal to her, including Mouse, her oldest Puma. - Minako kept the name, the cat, the cartoon, the Puma Squad under Tigress, the street contacts, and about six hundred people. She registered as Minako Arasaka, her legal birth name. The family has not sued.

The Pinkerton Cats

Minako doubled down on the cat girls. Every agent now wears pink-and-black armorjack and cat-ear sensor headsets with Kiroshi optics in the ears. Agents are Kittens, field teams of four or five are Prides, and the motto is "We Never Sleep" under a single wide-open cat's eye. Puma Squad: Nine Lives premiered the week of the Accord.

Danger Gal does missing persons, surveillance, bodyguarding, background checks and NCPD bounty work. It also takes a few cases a month that don't pay, for the people Minako used to work for in Kabuki, and those are the ones that go in the cartoon. And it watches Arasaka.

The Bridgehead

Danger Gal bought Whitewater Security's old eighteen-floor concrete headquarters in spring 2070 for a tenth of its value, with money borrowed from the Mox, when the Coronado Bay Bridge was on Militech's leaked demolition list. It sits between NCPD Precincts 1 and 3, ten minutes from both Downtown's paying clients and Kabuki's real ones. Every vehicle crossing the bridge passes its cameras, and a neon cat's eye on the north face stares across the bay at the Arasaka Waterfront all night. The lobby has a cat café that takes walk-ins.

Posted Rates, 2070

  • Background check: 100eb, one person, one day.
  • Missing person: 500eb plus 100eb a day. Most found within a week.
  • Surveillance: 200eb a day for a Kitten and a drone; a full Pride costs five times that.
  • Bodyguard: 500eb a day for two armed Kittens.
  • Bridge footage: 1,000eb for any vehicle that crossed the Coronado Bay Bridge in the last 30 days.

Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.05, 07; Danger Gal Dossier
